title: Staged handoff: shadow telemetry-driven staged handoff and automated rollback policy for mixed-mode deployments
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We need a consistent, low-friction process to promote model variants across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments that respects environment constraints (network, KMS, capacity) while preventing silent regressions. Current rollouts rely on ad-hoc canary percentages and manual checks; shadow traffic is inconsistently instrumented across environments, and rollbacks are manual or based on simple health checks.

Goal: Implement a staged handoff flow that uses shadow traffic telemetry to validate model behavior under real traffic, enable safe staged promotion (shadow -> live partial traffic -> progressive ramp), and trigger automatic, explainable rollbacks when predefined quality or latency regressions are detected. The system must handle environment-specific constraints: e.g., Private/VPC customers with on-premine GPUs may not support traffic mirroring at scale; Dedicated customers expect strict capacity guarantees; Hosted has the most flexible routing but also more heterogeneous tenant mixing.

Scope:
- Delivery of a sharable orchestration component (policy-driven) to define staged promotion plans and environment overrides.
- Telemetry schema for shadow comparisons (latency histograms, token-level error rates, output fidelity signals, divergence score against baseline, and per-tenant quality deltas).
- Rollback policy engine supporting immediate, threshold, and composite signals (latency, error rate, quality regression) with cooldown, dry-run, and explainability metadata.
- Operator console surfaces: per-rollout timeline, signal breakdowns, and suggested recovery actions.
- Implementation constraints for Private: a light-weight local agent to capture shadow telemetry and exchange summaries with control plane (no raw data exfiltration).

Non-goals: Full A/B experimentation framework for UX variants (this ticket focuses on model variant promotion and safety).

Design decisions and rationale:
1) Shadow telemetry aggregation: to respect PII and Private deployment constraints, raw example captures are disabled by default. Instead the local agent computes signed, deterministic feature hashes and summary metrics (percentiles, divergence buckets) and ships only aggregates to the control plane. This balances privacy/compliance and the need for cross-environment comparisons.
2) Composite rollback signal: single metric triggers are noisy. We define composite triggers with weights: 40% tail latency (p95/p99), 40% quality regression (evaluated using lightweight semantic similarity and domain-specific heuristics), 20% error/exception rate. A composite threshold breach will initiate a controlled rollback.
3) Staged handoff plan model: plans are first applied in shadow-only mode for N hours (configurable per environment), then live exposure ramps in steps (1%, 5%, 20%, 100%) with per-step hold windows and stability checks. Dedicated customers can request custom ramp schedules or request a bypass to skip shadowing if they already run internal validation.
4) Explainability: each auto-rollback action will produce a rollback rationale payload (metrics snapshot, recent diffs, a short textual explanation template) and a suggested mitigation list for on-call.

Acceptance criteria:
- New rollout policy entity available in control plane API and Redwood Console; users can create a staged handoff plan with environment overrides.
- Shadow telemetry schema defined and implemented for Hosted and Dedicated; local agent prototype for Private that produces aggregate telemetry summaries.
- Automated rollback engine executes test rollouts in staging and triggers rollback on composite breach; rollback actions and rationale viewable in console and emission of rollback event to incident stream.
- End-to-end tests demonstrating promotion from shadow -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with a simulated quality regression that triggers rollback at 5% step.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Finalize API surface and telemetry contract; design local agent summary format. Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/ENG-57911+Staged+Handoff+Design
- Week 2: Implement shadow telemetry pipeline for Hosted (server-side) and Dedicated (tenant isolated aggregation). Create telemetry dashboards (Grafana) and alert rules.
- Week 3: Build rollback policy engine (simulator mode) and integrate with runtime routing to flip traffic fractions. Add console UI wireframes.
- Week 4: Prototype local agent for Private deployments; run privacy review and security checklist.
- Week 5: Run canary promotion tests in staging, iterate on thresholds, add operator docs and runbooks.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Privacy vs signal fidelity: summary-only telemetry may hide rare failure modes visible only from raw examples. Mitigation: gated opt-in raw capture for Private customers with legal approval and explicit data retention controls.
- Complexity of composite signals: tuning weights and thresholds is non-trivial and depends on workload. We'll ship with conservative defaults and workflows to capture labeled postmortems for future ML-based threshold tuning.
- Private environment heterogeneity: local agent compatibility may require multiple packaging targets; initial scope focuses on Linux x86_64 and our supported on-prem GPU stacks.

Monitoring and observability:
- Dashboards: rollout-overview, per-rollout signal breakdown, per-tenant regressions, agent health.
- Alerts: rollback-triggered alert to on-call with severity mapping; trend alerts when multiple rollouts show correlated regressions.
- Tracing: correlation ids for shadow vs live requests to attribute regressions to specific model commit/revision.

Rollout steps and playbook (operator):
1) Create staged handoff plan via API or Console.
2) Execute in shadow mode for configured window. Monitor the shadow->baseline divergence dashboard.
3) If shadow metrics are stable, begin ramp to 1% with 30m hold. If composite metrics breach within hold, rollback automatically and notify.
4) After successful holds, proceed to next ramp. At any point, manual pause or rollback is supported.
